new.title: Slip into the walled Oude Hortus
new.desc: The university's old botanical garden hides behind a wall in the museum quarter. A centuries-old ginkgo and greenhouses with a giant Victoria water lily make it feel like a secret world in the middle of the city.
new.tip: It shares an entrance with the Universiteitsmuseum; finish with a coffee in the garden cafe.

new.title: Hear the street organs sing at Museum Speelklok
new.desc: Musical boxes, pianolas, carillon clocks and huge Dutch street organs fill a medieval church. The guides actually play them, so the visit is more concert than museum.
new.tip: Join one of the guided demonstrations; that is when the big organs are switched on.

new.title: Go under Domplein at DOMunder
new.desc: Below the square where the cathedral nave once stood lie the remains of the Roman fort that started Utrecht. A guided tour with a flashlight takes you through two thousand years of layers.
new.tip: Book a time slot in advance, and afterwards look at Domplein again knowing what lies under your feet.

new.title: Look up inside the old post office on Neude
new.desc: The 1924 main post office has a soaring hall of yellow brick parabolic arches and dark statues of the continents. Today it houses the city library, so you can simply walk in.
new.tip: Grab a seat on the upper floor of the library for the best view down into the great hall.

new.title: Meet Rietveld and Miffy at the Centraal Museum
new.desc: The oldest municipal museum in the country sits in a former medieval convent and holds the world's largest Rietveld collection, plus a look into Dick Bruna's studio.
new.tip: Lunch on the sunny terrace of Café Centraal, where the chairs are inspired by pieces in the collection.

new.title: Explore the treasures of Museum Catharijneconvent
new.desc: A former convent on the Nieuwegracht now shows a thousand years of Christian art in the Netherlands, from glittering medieval manuscripts to Reformation drama.
new.tip: Walk the quiet Nieuwegracht afterwards; it is the calmer twin of the Oudegracht.

new.title: Wander the old trees of Begraafplaats Soestbergen
new.desc: Utrecht's oldest general cemetery is a green, romantic park full of old trees and weathered graves, and a favourite quiet walk for locals.
new.tip: Enter from Gansstraat and take your time; it is a place to wander slowly and respectfully.

new.title: See painted wallpaper at Museum Oud Amelisweerd
new.desc: A country house in the Amelisweerd woods where hand-painted Asian wall hangings sit alongside modern art, a surprising mix in a quiet setting.
new.tip: Combine it with a walk along the Kromme Rijn; the house is on the edge of the woods.

new.title: Watch Molen De Ster saw timber by wind
new.desc: This 1721 sawmill at the edge of Lombok still turns logs into planks using only wind power, on the site of a historic timber yard.
new.tip: Come on a Saturday afternoon, when volunteers usually show visitors around.

new.title: Find the old station platform of Perron 9
new.desc: An 1893 platform canopy from Utrecht Centraal was saved and rebuilt on Berlijnplein in Leidsche Rijn, where it now shelters a square of new culture venues.
new.tip: Pair it with Castellum Hoge Woerd for a day of old structures in the newest part of the city.

new.title: Taste a Domtorentje at Theo Blom
new.desc: Since 1922 bakery Theo Blom has made Domtorentjes, big dark chocolate bonbons with a creamy filling and the Dom Tower stamped on top. They are the city's sweetest souvenir.
new.tip: Also pick up Bergman's Botersprits, slightly salty butter biscuits made to an 1888 Utrecht recipe.

new.title: Drink a Belgian beer in a church at Olivier
new.desc: Café Olivier fills a former church with long tables, an organ and a big menu of Belgian beers. It is one of the most atmospheric bars in town.
new.tip: Look up at the organ and order something you have never tried; the staff are happy to recommend.

new.title: Work through the list at Café België
new.desc: A narrow beer cafe on the Oudegracht with close to two hundred beers, including a long row of taps. Utrecht's beer lovers have been coming here for decades.
new.tip: Ask about the rotating draughts rather than the bottle list; that is where the surprises are.

new.title: Eat pancakes in De Oude Muntkelder
new.desc: A traditional Dutch pancake house in a vaulted wharf cellar right on the canal. Sweet or savoury, the pannenkoeken here are a Utrecht classic.
new.tip: Try a spekpannenkoek (bacon pancake) with stroop; students flock here early in the week.

new.title: Drink home-brewed beer on Boot 122
new.desc: One of three former brothel boats from the old Zandpad red-light quay is now a cosy beer bar that brews classic German-style beers. It is moored in the creative Werkspoorkwartier.
new.tip: Take the train to Utrecht Zuilen and rent an OV-fiets; the next boat over, EXboot, is a small gallery.

new.title: Share Asian plates at LE:EN in Rotsoord
new.desc: An Asian fusion restaurant with dishes for sharing, set in a former welding and construction hall by the Vaartsche Rijn. Industrial setting, lively vibe.
new.tip: Book ahead on weekends and walk back to the centre along the water.

new.title: Pick a beer from 160 at Jan Primus
new.desc: A neighbourhood brown cafe near Wilhelminapark with a famously long beer list, far from the tourist trail and loved by locals in the east of the city.
new.tip: Stroll through Wilhelminapark first and end with a drink here.

new.title: Grab a coffee at Koffie Leute Brauhaus
new.desc: A funky coffee house with graffiti, retro school chairs, vinyl and old video games, serving a different specialty coffee each month and vegan cake.
new.tip: It is a short walk from the station and the perfect start before exploring Lombok.
new.q: Leckere Koffie Leute Brauhaus Westerkade Utrecht

new.title: Roll with the Friday night Skate Parade
new.desc: On Friday evenings in the warmer months, a crowd of inline skaters takes over the streets for a free tour of around 20 kilometres through the city.
new.tip: It starts from Lucasbolwerk; check the weather and the group's announcements before you go.

new.title: Paddle the Oudegracht in a canoe
new.desc: Seeing the wharf cellars and low bridges from the water is a whole different city. You can rent a canoe on the canal itself and paddle under the medieval bridges.
new.tip: Head out in the morning before the tour boats get busy, and keep to the right.
new.q: Kanoverhuur Oudegracht aan de Werf Utrecht

new.title: Canoe out along the Kromme Rijn
new.desc: From the Rijnstroom rental you can paddle out of the city and along the winding Kromme Rijn past the woods of Amelisweerd and Rhijnauwen.
new.tip: Plan a pancake stop at Theehuis Rhijnauwen on the river bank before paddling back.

new.title: Look at the Sun from bastion Sonnenborgh
new.desc: A 19th-century observatory sits on top of a bastion built in 1552 for Emperor Charles V. Through one of the biggest solar telescopes in the country you can watch the surface of the Sun.
new.tip: Come to Sun on Sunday for the telescope, or book an English Stargazing Night in autumn or winter; they sell out fast.

new.title: Hear early music at Festival Oude Muziek
new.desc: Every late summer Utrecht hosts the world's leading festival for medieval, renaissance and baroque music, with concerts in the city's old churches.
new.tip: Look out for the free fringe concerts; hearing a lute in the Pieterskerk is pure magic.

new.title: Discover new sounds at Le Guess Who?
new.desc: In November this adventurous music festival fills TivoliVredenburg and venues across town with indie, experimental and global artists you have not heard yet.
new.tip: Even without a ticket, the free side programme around town is worth a wander.

new.title: Explore the makers of the Werkspoorkwartier
new.desc: An old factory district by the Amsterdam-Rijnkanaal turned creative hub: the Werkspoorkathedraal, artist studios at De Nijverheid, a gallery on a boat and a canal-side brewery bar.
new.tip: Start at Werkspoorcafé De Leckere behind the Werkspoorkathedraal, then walk along Nijverheidskade.

new.title: Visit Kasteel Amerongen, where the Kaiser abdicated
new.desc: A baroque castle on the Rhine in Amerongen, rebuilt after the French burned it in 1673. In 1918 the German Kaiser Wilhelm II signed his abdication here.
new.tip: Walk the historic gardens with the orangery; the village of Amerongen with its old tobacco barns is right outside the gate.

new.title: Step into the Kaiser's exile at Huis Doorn
new.desc: The last German Emperor spent his final years in this manor in Doorn, and his rooms, uniforms and treasures are still there as he left them.
new.tip: Leave time for the park, where Wilhelm II is buried in a small mausoleum. Bus from Driebergen-Zeist station.

new.title: See where Mondriaan was born in Amersfoort
new.desc: Piet Mondriaan's birthplace on the Kortegracht tells the story of his work and has a reconstruction of his 1920s Paris studio.
new.tip: From here it is a few minutes to the Koppelpoort and the Muurhuizen.

new.title: Find the Amersfoortse Kei
new.desc: A huge glacial boulder that locals once dragged into town as a joke, then buried in shame. Dug up in 1903, it became the proud symbol of the city, whose people are still called Keientrekkers.
new.tip: Follow the ring road and spot the boulders other cities sent as gifts.

new.title: Find the quiet Hofje Armen de Poth in Amersfoort
new.desc: A small medieval almshouse courtyard in the heart of Amersfoort, an unexpected oasis of calm a few steps from the shopping streets.
new.tip: Residents live here, so keep your voice down and visit during the day.

new.title: See Ruisdael's mill in Wijk bij Duurstede
new.desc: Windmill Rijn en Lek stands on top of a 14th-century city gate, the only Dutch mill built on one. It is known as the Mill of Ruisdael after the famous painting of a mill in this town.
new.tip: Volunteer millers usually grind on Wednesday and Saturday afternoons. In summer, cycle here from Utrecht along the Kromme Rijn.
new.q: Molen Rijn en Lek Wijk bij Duurstede

new.title: Pay respects at the Grebbeberg war cemetery
new.desc: On the hill above Rhenen lie some 800 soldiers who fell in May 1940 defending the Grebbe line against the German invasion, many on the very spot where they fought.
new.tip: Walk on through the woods of the Grebbeberg for views over the Rhine floodplain.

new.title: Stroll the Dorpsstraat of Loenen aan de Vecht
new.desc: A protected village with 144 listed monuments, a long main street along the Vecht, country estates built by Amsterdam merchants and a church tower that leans about 80 cm.
new.tip: Get here by bike along the Vecht from Breukelen; the estates are best seen from the water side.

new.title: Walk around Sanatorium Zonnestraal in Hilversum
new.desc: A 1920s sanatorium of glass and white concrete in the woods south of Hilversum, a landmark of modernist architecture with a walking trail through the estate.
new.tip: Follow the 4.5 km trail through Loosdrechtse Bos to see the buildings from every angle.

new.title: Eat a pancake in Lage Vuursche
new.desc: Wealthy Baarn families came to this forest hamlet for giant pancakes as early as the 19th century. Pannenkoekenhuis De Vuursche Boer, open since 1959, has baked millions of them.
new.tip: Make it the reward after a forest walk past Kasteel Drakensteyn; in good weather the terrace fills up quickly.

new.title: Taste farmhouse cheese at the Woerden cheese market
new.desc: Woerden calls itself the true cheese town of the Netherlands. On summer Saturday mornings the Kerkplein fills with boerenkaas, handjeklap bargaining and weighing, ending with a historic market in late August.
new.tip: Buy a piece of aged boerenkaas to take home, then visit the Kaaspakhuis on the Emmakade. Woerden station is a ten-minute walk.

new.title: Dine inside the Monnickendam water gate in Amersfoort
new.desc: The southern water gate of Amersfoort's second city wall now has a restaurant inside, so you eat between medieval walls above the canal.
new.tip: Walk the canal from the Koppelpoort to Monnickendam to see both water gates in one go.

new.title: Graze the food hall of Mout in Hilversum
new.desc: On the market square, Mout combines an Asian-style food court with its own local brewery, a relaxed place to eat in the media town.
new.tip: Combine it with Dudok's town hall, a short walk away.

new.title: Have lunch at Restaurant Abrona in Oudewater
new.desc: Many of the staff at this hotel restaurant are people with disabilities, and visitors praise both the warm service and the food.
new.tip: Combine it with the Heksenwaag and the small rope museum De Baanschuur in town.

new.title: Spot birds on the Leersumse Veld
new.desc: Heath, woods and ponds near Leersum on the Utrechtse Heuvelrug, grazed by cattle and home to black woodpeckers, wood larks and, in winter, the great grey shrike.
new.tip: Follow the yellow 6 km route and sit in the covered bird hide by the ponds; parking is on the Maarsbergseweg.

new.title: Climb Lange Jan in Amersfoort
new.desc: The 98 metre Onze Lieve Vrouwetoren, nicknamed Lange Jan, towers over the old town and can be seen from far across the Eemland.
new.tip: Guided climbs of 364 steps run in summer; book at the tourist office right next to the tower.

new.title: Walk the drift sands of the Soesterduinen
new.desc: Some 500 hectares of open drifting sand and juniper south of Soest, among the last big open sand dunes on the Utrechtse Heuvelrug. Trees were cleared so the wind can move the sand again.
new.tip: Soest Zuid station is right at the edge; go barefoot on the Lange Duinen on a warm day.

new.title: Play TV at Beeld en Geluid in Hilversum
new.desc: Hilversum is the home of Dutch broadcasting, and the Netherlands Institute for Sound and Vision is its interactive media museum, wrapped in a building with a colourful glass facade.
new.tip: Try presenting the news or a weather report in the studios. It is a short walk from Hilversum Media Park station.

new.title: Get out on the water at the Loosdrechtse Plassen
new.desc: These lakes were dug out by centuries of peat cutting until the strips of land between them washed away. Today they are a big playground for sailing, swimming and boating.
new.tip: Rent a whisper boat or sloop in Oud-Loosdrecht; the Vijfde Plas is the spot for swimming.

new.title: Climb the Cunera tower in Rhenen
new.desc: The late Gothic Cunerakerk tower rises high above the Rhine town of Rhenen and the river landscape, with the Grebbeberg on one side and the Betuwe on the other.
new.tip: Buy tower tickets at the tourist office; the church itself is free to look into.
